title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false positive in an automated license-plate reader that became an armed stop. The system misread a character, matched a plate to a similar stolen vehicle, and the resulting alert was treated by a deputy as grounds to hold a person at gunpoint. The failure sits at the handoff between the automated alert and the human decision to enforce.

The check that would have caught it is the one Flock itself describes, an independent verification of the alert before officers take enforcement action. The sheriff's office instead called the deputy's actions reasonable and attributed the error to a tinted plate cover. That attribution is the agency's account, not an established cause.

What is not established is whether the plate cover was illegal or actually caused the misread, and no ruling on the deputy's conduct has been reported. A single outlet's report is not proof of intent, and the sheriff's characterization is not a finding.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was held at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office later said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the error and called the deputy’s actions reasonable. Flock said alerts should be checked independently before officers take enforcement action.
title_en: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover
